敗之餘乞粗存活便足慰吾餘

老奴果如所卜
玉鏡臺

review.explanation: The mention 王隱 appears in annotation 003 as '王隱晉書曰', which is the standard way of citing the Jin dynasty historian 王隱's work 王隱晉書. The surface form is the full canonical name, and the context of a Liu Xiaobiao annotation citing a historical work directly supports identification with the historian 王隱. The evidence specifically names 王隱 as the author of the cited work, which is a direct identity assertion.

The mention 琨 appears in annotation 004: '琨假守左司馬都督上前鋒諸軍事討劉聦'. This describes Liu Kun (劉琨) holding the office of 假守左司馬都督上前鋒諸軍事 and attacking 劉聦. The historical role of Liu Kun as a Jin general who campaigned against Liu Cong (劉聦) is well-documented, and the annotation explicitly names 琨 in this role. The evidence directly supports the identification with 劉琨.

The mention 嶠 appears in the main text as the person 温公 refers to himself ('如嶠比'), and in annotation 003 as '嶠為劉...'. The main text establishes 温公 as the protagonist who seeks a bride, and the annotation identifies 嶠 as serving under 劉 (劉琨). The alias registry identifies 温公 as 温嶠, and the coreference between 温公 and 嶠 in the main text is clear. The evidence directly supports the identification.

The mention 劉越石 appears in the main text: '是公為劉越石長史北征劉聦所得'. 劉越石 is the courtesy name (字) of 劉琨. The text states that 温公 (嶠) served as 長史 under 劉越石 during a northern campaign against 劉聦. This matches the historical record that 温嶠 served under 劉琨. The alias registry confirms 劉越石 as a form of 劉琨's name, and the historical context of the campaign against 劉聦 corroborates this identification.

The mention surface is 嶠, which is the personal name of 温嶠. The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-009-main) explicitly uses 嶠 in the phrase '如嶠比' and '不減嶠' referring to the protagonist 温公. The alias registry evidence provides the contextual title 温公 for 温嶠. The identity is directly supported by the personal name 嶠 matching 温嶠's given name, and the annotation explicitly ties this 嶠 to 温氏譜 (Wen family genealogy). No contradicting evidence exists.

The mention surface is 劉 (surname-only). The main text states '公為劉越石長史' — 温公 served as 長史 under 劉越石, and 劉越石 is the courtesy name of 劉琨. The surname 劉 in this context refers to 劉琨, as the main text establishes 温公's service under 劉越石 (=劉琨). The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-d3d2943f51ca337e10fc) shows the surface 琨 from the annotation, directly matching 劉琨's personal name. This is a surname-only reference to 劉琨, and the contextual evidence from both the main text and annotations supports this identification.

The mention surface is 温公, which is the office-title reference to 温嶠. The alias registry evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-1d3448186f9b2ee8e5df) explicitly maps 温公 to 温嶠. records.explanation: 温公 is the office-title reference to 温嶠 (Wen Qiao). The main text describes him as having lost his wife and having a paternal aunt (從姑) surnamed 劉. The name 嶠 appears later in the text (mention b111c0c535e68cbda0013acd) referring to the same person. The 姑 (paternal aunt) is distinct from 温公.
records.referent_role: 温嶠 (Wen Qiao), referred to by his office title 温公

records.explanation: 載 is stated as an alternate name (一名) for 聦 in the annotation: 聦一名載字玄明. Thus 載, 聦, and 玄明 all refer to the same person, Liu Cong.
records.referent_role: ruler/leader of the Xiongnu (Liu Cong), alternate name

records.explanation: 女 is a kinship reference meaning daughter of 琅邪王詡. The annotation states 琅邪王詡女後取廬江何䆳女, meaning the daughter of 琅邪王詡 was later taken (married) by 嶠, and then 嶠 took the daughter of 廬江何䆳.
records.referent_role: daughter of 琅邪王詡, later married to 嶠

reviews.explanation: The mention 王隱 appears in annotation 003 as '王隱晉書曰', which is the standard way of citing the Jin dynasty historian 王隱's work 王隱晉書. The surface form is the full canonical name, and the context of a Liu Xiaobiao annotation citing a historical work directly supports identification with the historian 王隱. The evidence specifically names 王隱 as the author of the cited work, which is a direct identity assertion.

The mention 琨 appears in annotation 004: '琨假守左司馬都督上前鋒諸軍事討劉聦'. This describes Liu Kun (劉琨) holding the office of 假守左司馬都督上前鋒諸軍事 and attacking 劉聦. The historical role of Liu Kun as a Jin general who campaigned against Liu Cong (劉聦) is well-documented, and the annotation explicitly names 琨 in this role. The evidence directly supports the identification with 劉琨.

The mention 嶠 appears in the main text as the person 温公 refers to himself ('如嶠比'), and in annotation 003 as '嶠為劉...'. The main text establishes 温公 as the protagonist who seeks a bride, and the annotation identifies 嶠 as serving under 劉 (劉琨). The alias registry identifies 温公 as 温嶠, and the coreference between 温公 and 嶠 in the main text is clear. The evidence directly supports the identification.

The mention 劉越石 appears in the main text: '是公為劉越石長史北征劉聦所得'. 劉越石 is the courtesy name (字) of 劉琨. The text states that 温公 (嶠) served as 長史 under 劉越石 during a northern campaign against 劉聦. This matches the historical record that 温嶠 served under 劉琨. The alias registry confirms 劉越石 as a form of 劉琨's name, and the historical context of the campaign against 劉聦 corroborates this identification.

The mention surface is 嶠, which is the personal name of 温嶠. The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-009-main) explicitly uses 嶠 in the phrase '如嶠比' and '不減嶠' referring to the protagonist 温公. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-009-liu-annotation-001) explicitly states '按温氏譜嶠初取髙平李暅女中取琅邪王詡女後取廬江何䆳女', confirming that 嶠 in the annotation refers to 温嶠. The alias registry evidence provides the contextual title 温公 for 温嶠. The identity is directly supported by the personal name 嶠 matching 温嶠's given name, and the annotation explicitly ties this 嶠 to 温氏譜 (Wen family genealogy). No contradicting evidence exists.

The mention surface is 劉 (surname-only). The main text states '公為劉越石長史' — 温公 served as 長史 under 劉越石, and 劉越石 is the courtesy name of 劉琨. The Liu annotation 003 reads '嶠為劉...' referring to the same relationship. Annotation 004 explicitly mentions '琨假守左司馬都督上前鋒諸軍事討劉聦', confirming 琨 (劉琨) is the person being discussed. The surname 劉 in this context refers to 劉琨, as the main text establishes 温公's service under 劉越石 (=劉琨). The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-d3d2943f51ca337e10fc) shows the surface 琨 from the annotation, directly matching 劉琨's personal name. This is a surname-only reference to 劉琨, and the contextual evidence from both the main text and annotations supports this identification.

The mention surface is 温公, which is the office-title reference to 温嶠. The alias registry evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-1d3448186f9b2ee8e5df) explicitly maps 温公 to 温嶠. The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-009-main) describes 温公 as the protagonist who lost his wife and sought a new marriage, and later the text uses 嶠 to refer to the same person ('如嶠比', '不減嶠'), confirming 温公 = 嶠 = 温嶠. The main text also states '公為劉越石長史', which is consistent with 温嶠's historical role. The reference semantics correctly identify this as an office_holder_reference. No contradicting evidence exists.

assertions.interpretation: A few days after the aunt's reply, Wen Gong reported he had found a match.
After the wedding ceremony and exchange of rites, the woman lifted her veil and laughed.
The Liu family was scattered during the period of chaos and disorder, which is the background context for the aunt entrusting her daughter to Wen Gong.
The aunt describes the aftermath of defeat and loss, indicating the family's reduced circumstances at the time of the matchmaking.

assertions.interpretation: Liu Xiaobiao's annotation cites Wang Yin's Jin shu noting that in the second year (of a reign era) Qiao served under Liu (Kun), providing reign-era context for his office.
Liu Cong's father Liu Yuan raised troops amid the chaos and died; Cong succeeded him — background on Liu Cong's rise relevant to the northern campaign.
According to the Wen family genealogy, Qiao first married the daughter of Li Hui of Gaoping, then married (another) — background on his marital history.
